text:
customer_acme: Hey team — during a live demo to a partner our org (acme-int) dropped to 0 credits around 17:02 and all streaming calls started returning 429s. We were nowhere near expected monthly usage. Can you investigate?

sara_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error you saw? Was it a 429 with "quota exceeded" or something else?

customer_acme: It was a 429 JSON: `\{"error\":\"quota_exhausted\", \"detail\":\"monthly bucket empty\"\}`. The UI also showed 0/1,000,000 tokens for the org. Demo started at 16:30 and we had ~200k tokens left based on dashboard refresh at 15:50.

mike_billing: On it. Two quick Qs: which org did you use (org id or slug) and what timezone is your account set to? Also did you have any other projects under the same org that could have consumed tokens?

customer_acme: Org slug `acme-int` (we have prod `acme` and demo `acme-int` under same billing account). Account timezone is America/Chicago. We only used demo instance for the meeting — one long streaming call to live-capture a transcript + summarization.

raj_eng: Can you share a rough sequence length / tokens per minute for the streaming session? Streaming double-counting can look like depletion if clients reconnect a lot.

customer_acme: Transcript stream was ~600 tokens/minute, participants were reconnecting once around 16:50 (meeting signal blip) but resumed quickly. Not thousands of reconnects.

mike_billing: I'm checking billing-side usage. I see a sharp spike for `acme-int` between 16:58 and 17:03 that perfectly matches your 429 window — but the tokens are counted against the parent billing org because the demo org is on consolidated billing. That spike looks like a single large batch event of ~820k tokens. Can you confirm if you ran any batch exports, replays, or long eval runs at that time?

customer_acme: No exports scheduled. The only thing was our demo script that replayed a saved conversation when network hiccup happened — but that should have been a couple minutes. Not 820k.

raj_eng: Possible causes: 1) replay accidentally looping (client bug), 2) server-side duplicate crediting due to retry proto issues, or 3) a quota aggregation mismatch where parent org showed combined usage with prod.

sara_support: For immediate relief we can temporarily top up the monthly bucket for `acme-int` to unblock you for the rest of the demo. Recommend we do that while we root-cause. @mike_billing can you approve a one-off credit?

mike_billing: Approved. Pushing 1,000,000 token grant to org `acme-int` now. Should reflect within ~30s. ops-bot:billing_action log: `grant 1000000 tokens to acme-int by mike_billing`

ops-bot:billing_action: timestamp=1732102760 action=grant org=acme-int amount=1000000 actor=mike_billing

customer_acme: Confirmed — calls resumed, thanks. We finished the demo.

mike_billing: Next steps for RCA: I'm going to pull the per-project ingestion logs and look for duplicate ingest IDs or any large replay jobs from 16:45-17:10. raj_eng can you look at the serving logs for duplicate request IDs and whether a client reconnect could have caused the runtime to not drop caches and re-process tokens?

raj_eng: Will do. Also will check routing logs to see if requests were routed to the parent billing pool mistakenly (we had a recent canary change around consolidated-billing routing last week). If the route merged usage windows incorrectly it could have double-counted for both `acme` and `acme-int`.

sara_support: FYI for timeline: we did a quick surface-level check — no scheduled housekeeping jobs, no org-wide evals on record. The 820k spike is anomalous.

mike_billing: I see an entry in the billing ingestion pipeline: `ingest_batch_id=ing-20260321-1158` with `duplicate_flag=true` and `retry_count=2`. That suggests the batch accounting job retried and re-applied usage. We're investigating how dedupe failed.

raj_eng: If batch accounting retried without idempotency, that explains double-charge. We need to verify whether the retry window overlapped an earlier successful run. I'll trace request lineage back to the runtime logs.

customer_acme: We'd like a postmortem and assurance this won't happen again — demo was with a partner and that was embarrassing.

sara_support: Absolutely. We'll compile a short incident note once we have the RCA. Immediate item: mike_billing to open a support billing ticket to roll back the duplicate charges and issue a formal credit. raj_eng to patch the dedupe logic + add metric alert for >50% token spike in 5min window.

mike_billing: Ticket created: #BILL-5921. Rolling back duplicate ingestion and issuing a credit for 820k tokens. Sending update to `customer_acme` once done.

raj_eng: Patch in progress — adding idempotency checks (ingest_batch_id uniqueness) and an alert (SpikeTokens5m) in console. Will also add an internal runbook step to check consolidated billing vs per-org mapping during spikes.

sara_support: I'll follow up with the customer with a summary and ETA for the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

customer_acme: Thanks — appreciate the quick top-up and the follow-up. Please include whether account timezone offsets affected the reset timing — we had thought a reset might have fallen earlier because of DST, but sounds like duplicate accounting is more likely based on your logs.
